newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Adelaide Brighton sees profit rise.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Adelaide Brighton sees profit rise.

text.p: Cement maker Adelaide Brighton Ltd said on Wednesday it expected earnings for the year to June 30, 1997 to be ahead of 1995/96 but below its budget.

The company said there were indications that Australian construction markets were beginning to strengthen, with evidence of an improvement in housing starts and stready growth in infrastructure and commercial construction as well.
"The group's operational focus will be to ensure that production, marketing and administrative activities are improved so as to take full advantage of this upturn," it said.
"However, profits for the year to date are below budget and while directors expect full year earnings to be ahead of last year, they are not expected to meet this year's budget."
Adelaide Brighton reported a net loss of A$49.26 million in 1995/96 compared with a 1994/95 loss of A$31.40 million.
Last year's loss included a A$47.78 million extraordinary loss on the sale of the Gunpowder copper project.
Operating profit in 1995/96 was A$26.0 million.
The company said in a statement accompanying the first half results that it had taken some major steps to improve its gearing and to focus on the development of the core business.

It said its board on Wednesday approved a A$15.3 million investment in the construction of a quicklime kiln at Kwinana in Western Australia and the purchase of the assets and business of bagged cement company Melcann Ltd in the same state.
It did not reveal the purchase price for the Melcann assets.
"The development of the group's regional strategy is undergoing a rigorous review and progress in this area can be expected over the next year or two," the company said.
